title: Learning a Continuous Sepsis Severity Score Without Hour-by-Hour Supervision: A Two-Site Retrospective Study
abstract: arXiv:2608.27421v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Currently used sepsis severity indices rely on fixed variables and weights established decades ago, which are coarsely discretized and calibrated to a cohort that no longer reflects contemporary critical care. No alternative learned directly from patient trajectories is in routine use. We conducted a retrospective two-cohort study on a total of 29,116 and 7,691 adult patients meeting Sepsis-3 criteria from two hospital systems in Massachusetts and Georgie, respectively.   We developed a sepsis index using 43 routinely charted variables over a 72-hour treatment window. Unlike previous studies, we use mortality as a treatment-level ranking signal rather than a per-state target, allowing credit to be redistributed non-uniformly across timesteps. Evaluation was done on a permanent 20% test holdout, using clinical vignettes and Spearman correlation. Uncertainty intervals were obtained by bootstrap resampling of whole patients. Under this rank

translated_title: 学习无需逐小时监督的连续脓毒症严重程度评分：一项双中心回顾性研究
translated_abstract: arXiv:2608.27421v1 公告类型：新 摘要：目前使用的脓毒症严重程度指数依赖于几十年前确定的固定变量和权重，这些变量被粗略离散化，并校准到不再反映当代重症监护的队列中。没有直接从患者轨迹中学习的替代方法在常规使用中。我们对来自马萨诸塞州和佐治亚州两个医院系统的29,116名和7,691名符合Sepsis-3标准的成年患者进行了回顾性双队列研究。我们使用43个常规记录的变量在72小时治疗窗口内开发了一种脓毒症指数。与之前的研究不同，我们将死亡率作为治疗水平的排序信号，而非逐状态目标，允许信用在时间步长上非均匀地重新分配。评估在永久性的20%测试保留集上进行，使用临床小插图和Spearman相关性。不确定性区间通过自助重采样整个患者获得。在此排序下...
tldr: 本研究提出了一种利用患者轨迹和死亡率排序信号，在无需逐小时监督的情况下，连续学习脓毒症严重程度评分的新方法，并在两个大型医院系统数据上进行了验证。
en_tdlr: This study proposes a novel method to continuously learn a sepsis severity score from patient trajectories using mortality as a ranking signal without hour-by-hour supervision, validated on two large hospital system datasets.
